abstract: This tutorial discusses the methods used to make the fundamental measurement of phase, and building from that foundation goes on to discuss frequency, MTIE, and TDEV calculations and their interpretation. Following this theoretical introduction, a number of measurements taken in live networks throughout the world representing diverse conditions are interpreted and discussed.

abstract: This paper provides an overview of the current and future applications which will requires syntonization and synchronization in telecom networks. The key idea of this presentation is to depict the differences of the requirements in terms of synchronization (e.g. frequency, phase, time-of-day, corresponding accuracies…). The other main aspect of this paper is to address the architecture challenges that an operator will have to deal with in the near future. Indeed, the network is changing, new network technologies start to appear, and different cases will probably imply the use of different methods to deliver the required synchronization. The idea is here to depict the potential solutions and mechanisms that can be used depending on the different architecture cases and application requirements.

abstract: The paper presents an overview of the 3GPP Mobile Broadcast and Multicast Service (MBMS) and of MBMS over a Single Frequency Network (MBSFN). It deals MBSFN network/content synchronisation issues and design of a suitable network protocol.

abstract: This paper examines a range of issues relating to synchronization of multimedia applications over wireless networks which are becoming very prevalent in the home. In particular we look at VoIP and audiophile quality speaker synchronization. Although very different in terms of user requirements, they both can benefit greatly from time and timing synchronization.

abstract: Scalability with guaranteed performance are emerging as central for the viability of the Internet continuous growth in capacity, services and number of nodes. This talk focuses on two critical problems: (1) cost reduction (equipment and transmission) and (2) performance guarantees that are independent of the network size and instant traffic load. It is shown that by using global time it is possible and simple to provide effective solutions.

abstract: This paper presents the work being carried out by Vodafone to assess whether IEEE 1588v2 can provide a ubiquitous solution fulfilling the synchronization requirements of current and future Vodafone mobile networks over different backhaul technologies and traffic loads. The results of IEEE 1588v2 lab tests performed with a mix of IP/MPLS over Ethernet and SHDSL/ADSL transport are analysed and the main conclusions drawn. The paper also describes the necessary future steps in IEEE 1588v2 to enable its widespread adoption by mobile operators.

abstract: This talk will provide an overview of Multi-Protocol Label Switching (MPLS). We will describe some of the background to and history of MPLS, together with some of the key data and control plane mechanisms used by MPLS. We will then move on to explain how MPLS is used to support new applications such as Layer 3 and Layer 2 VPNs over a converged IP network infrastructure. These applications require the traffic engineering, QoS and resiliency that MPLS provides, and can also be used to support services for which synchronization is a critical requirement.

abstract: GALILEO is Europe’s initiative for a state-of-the-art global navigation satellite system, providing a highly accurate, guaranteed global positioning, navigation and timing service under civilian control. In addition of the Open Services which will provide GNSS performances free of charge but without any guarantee of service, the Public Regulated Service (PRS) will provide position and timing to specific users requiring a high continuity of service and integrity, thanks to its improved robustness to interference and jamming and its incorporated integrity feature. Two PRS navigation signals with encrypted ranging codes and data will be available. The European GNSS Supervisory Authority and an EADS-led consortium have been managing since September 2006 the first PRS project, entitled PACIFIC standing for “PRS Application Concept Involving Future Interested Customers”. The main objective of this project is to pave the way towards the introduction of Galileo PRS into User Communities to enable them to benefit from the added value of the Galileo PRS capabilities, whatever they use the GNSS capability for navigation, positioning or timing applications. The PACIFIC presentation will set out the following points: ▪ Status on the Galileo Programme to date ; ▪ Results of the PACIFIC project so far including the definition of the benefits and added value to users of the Galileo PRS; ▪ Role of Galileo PRS in synchronisation & timing applications, in particular by providing a reliable synchronization facility through its continuity of service and its integrity feature. It is anticipated that by the time of the conference detailed results will be available from detailed interactions with user communities to identify the benefits to them that Galileo PRS can bring. Also available at this time will be information about the key technology challenges in Galileo PRS User equipment and the infrastructure that will be necessary to enable users to use Galileo PRS.
